item.description: Beyond Individual AI Tasks Blackwell distinguished the current generation of AI automation from the broader agentic model Applied is developing. The ‘Current of Insurance’ Blackwell summarized the larger strategy through Applied’s new description of itself as “the current of insurance.” The phrase captures Applied’s ambition to connect the work performed inside agencies with the information and decisions moving between agencies and carriers. item.title: AI Pricing Lawsuit Against McDonald’s Raises New Antitrust Questions
item.description: A federal antitrust lawsuit against McDonald’s this week claims the fast-food giant is using AI-powered tools to fix menu prices, marking the latest case to allege companies are relying on new technologies to collude and harm consumers. However, antitrust law can bar businesses that compete against each other from using such tools to coordinate their decision-making when it raises consumer costs. It says restaurant owners should be competing freely but are pressured by McDonald’s to use its “pricing engine” or risk losing their franchise status, driving up the cost of Big Macs, fries and other menu items for millions of customers.

item.title: Why Your Boss Matters More Than Remote or Hybrid Work When It Comes to Burnout and Job Satisfaction
item.description: The post-pandemic push to bring workers back to the office has left many nostalgic for more flexible arrangements , such as hybrid or remote work. But a wealth of data since the pandemic now suggests that workplace factors like feeling appreciated and having a good relationship with your manager are much more tied to job satisfaction than the actual time spent in the office. The workplace behind the work arrangement Semi- or fully remote workers may appear more satisfied .

item.title: Be Mindful: How Workplace Hierarchy Can Shape Even Positive Interactions
item.description: In the workplace, sharing positive, work-related news can have very different effects on the people involved depending on where they sit in the organizational hierarchy, according to research led by Emily Poulton , assistant professor of management at the Indiana University Kelley School of Business Indianapolis. Have you ever found yourself listening to someone share their good news and felt pressure to respond with excitement, even if you didn’t feel particularly enthusiastic? Does that pressure feel even greater when the person sharing the news is your boss?

item.title: The Latest Launches from The Zebra, Sigo Seguros, Applied Systems
item.description: Sigo Seguros, a licensed insurance agency built for Hispanic and working-class families, announced its expansion into commercial auto insurance, starting in Texas on October 1, 2026. Contractors, delivery drivers, and other business owners who work from their trucks and vans can now request a quote on Sigo Seguros’ website. A licensed Sigo Seguros agent will help them understand their options and compare coverage from multiple carriers.

item.title: CyberCube finds 300 Russia-linked cyber incidents against UK companies since 2022
item.description: More than 300 Russia-linked cyber incidents have affected UK-headquartered companies since 2022, according to CyberCube data cited in a new report on the economic cost of Russian hostile activity against the UK. CyberCube’s findings, featured in The Putin Tax: Estimating the Economic Cost of Russian Hostile Activity Against the United Kingdom , published by Labour MP Graeme Downie with Dr Dominic Reed. The report describes itself as the first attempt to measure the economic burden of Russian hostile activity on the UK, covering cyber attacks, sabotage and threats against critical infrastructure.

item.title: Texas Agency Sues to Stop Release of Data Center Records, Citing Terrorist Risk
item.description: The Public Utility Commission of Texas is asking a Travis County judge to block the release of information showing where data centers and virtual currency mines operate, saying those details could aid terrorists. The lawsuit filed Monday pits the state agency responsible for regulating utilities against Attorney General Ken Paxton’s office over the scope of Texas’ public-records law and the state’s protections for critical infrastructure. But it does come as Texas officials are seeking more information about the state’s data center industry.

item.title: Ohio Contractor Sued for for Alleged Incomplete Home Improvements
item.description: Ohio Attorney General Andy Wilson is suing a home-improvement contractor in southwestern Ohio accused of charging consumers for services that were not completed or, in some cases, even started. Wilson’s lawsuit alleges that Cincinnati-based Quincy Barrett and his company, Crown Pointe Remodeling, solicited consumers online and sold home improvement services, including interior remodeling and repair work as well as roofing, siding, windows and other exterior work. But consumers who filed complaints with the Ohio Attorney General’s Office say the defendants charged large upfront payments and didn’t complete or start the jobs.

item.title: California Workers’ Comp Combined Ratio Highest in More Than 20 Years
item.description: The projected combined ratio for California workers’ compensation insurers reached 127% in 2025, the highest in more than 20 years, a new report shows. Related: Report: Medical Service Costs in California Comp Rising With Payments, Utilization Written premium in the first six months of 2026 was 5% higher than during the same period in 2025. The Workers’ Compensation Insurance Rating Bureau of California released its latest Quarterly Experience Report , which delves into insurer experience through June 30.

item.title: Zillion partners with Tokio Marine Highland
item.description: Zillion has partnered with Tokio Marine Highland to offer embedded insurance for luxury jewelry and watches through its network of retailers, brands, appraisers, and collector applications. Tokio Marine Highland is a specialty managing general agency and a wholly owned subsidiary of Tokio Marine Kiln. Zillion says it has protected billions of dollars’ worth of luxury items through its partner network.

item.title: Meanwhile raises $37.5 million
item.description: Bermuda-based Bitcoin life insurer Meanwhile has raised $37.5 million from existing investors, bringing its total funding to more than $180 million. Earlier this year, Meanwhile launched BTC Life 1-Pay, a single-premium whole life policy for high-net-worth clients outside the US. Meanwhile has signed 15 brokers serving wealthy families, including Lioner and Apeiron Group, with distribution spanning Singapore, Hong Kong, the UAE, and Switzerland.

item.title: Coverdash launches Claude connector for business insurance
item.description: Digital business insurance agency Coverdash has launched a Claude connector that lets eligible policyholders access and manage their commercial insurance through the AI assistant. The integration extends Coverdash’s embedded insurance approach into policy servicing, bringing tasks typically handled through an insurance portal or an agent into a conversational interface. The company says the connector is intended to complement the insurance professionals supporting its customers.

item.title: Europe Posted Its Strongest Quarter In Q3 In 4 Years, As Its Venture Ecosystem Expands Beyond The UK
item.description: In Q3, Europe posted its strongest venture funding quarter in four years, with AI companies driving those gains, Crunchbase data shows. continued to lead startup funding totals last quarter, Germany and France both posted their strongest quarters since the boom years of 2021 and early 2022. Last quarter’s funding totals were boosted heavily by a $3.5 billion investment in Paris-based Mistral , the largest venture round ever for a Europe-based company.

item.title: Hurricane Isaias strengthens, ~Cat 2 landfall at single-digit billion insured loss potential forecast
item.description: Isaiais is now the first hurricane of the 2026 Atlantic season having intensified overnight and the forecast continues to suggest a Category 2 landfall on the Gulf Coast is a possible outcome, at which level of intensity reinsurance broker Gallagher Re said it would typically result in insured losses in the low to mid-single digit billions. The chart below from Tomer Burg’s PolarWx service shows the current NHC forecast including cone and wind speeds (this should update to show the latest hurricane information shortly): Impacts from hurricane Isaias will be more widely felt than just the cone, with high rainfall levels expected more broadly along the Gulf Coast, as well as inland along hurricane Isaias’ track after it makes landfall and there are warnings of tornado potential with this storm as well. New NHC forecast advisory data continues to suggest hurricane Isaias may have sustained winds of around 95 knots at its peak, close to 110 mph, but the forecast for slight weakening before landfall also remains.

item.title: Higher short-term rates boost ILS returns, reshape hedge fund attribution: Agecroft’s Steinbrugge
item.description: Steinbrugge notes that while investors tend to associate rising rates with declining asset values, the impact on hedge fund strategies is more nuanced, particularly as some strategies can benefit from higher short-term rates, while others may encounter higher financing costs that can materially reduce returns. Higher short-term interest rates are providing an additional source of return for ILS, while also reshaping strategy-level return attribution across the hedge fund industry. In addition, Steinbrugge underscores that quantitative hedge funds may also benefit from the return of meaningful short-term interest rates.

item.title: Reask to provide settlement data for Interactive Brokers’ ForecastEx live hurricane contracts
item.description: Interactive Brokers’ ForecastEx platform has partnered with Reask, the catastrophe modelling and climate analytics specialist, which will see Reask supply settlement data for its live hurricane contracts, enabling capital providers to enter and exit live catastrophe exposure in real time. Interactive Brokers’ ForecastEx has listed a new class of tradeable event contracts, referred to as live hurricane contracts, that are tied to wind gusts produced by individual named storms at specific coastal locations. The new live hurricane contracts on ForecastEx propose to transfer the same category of risk, structured as exchange-traded, continuously priced instruments rather than bilateral “off-line” agreements.” Reask continued: “Looking back historically, the Chicago Mercantile Exchange (CME) has offered tradeable hurricane contracts based on a storm-wide index.

item.title: UK insurers face margin pressures despite resilient revenue outlook: Moody’s
item.description: Moody’s Ratings forecasts that UK insurers will continue to generate revenue growth in 2027 even as unemployment increases and inflation remains relatively persistent. Moody’s Ratings, the credit ratings agency, expects the outlook for the UK’s life and property and casualty (P&C) insurance sectors to remain stable. The agency says insurers should continue to benefit from strong sources of revenue, including higher investment yields, growing pension savings and consistent demand for compulsory insurance.

item.title: Sapiens launches insurance-native AI foundation powering SapiensAIP
item.description: Sapiens International Corporation N.V., a provider of AI-centric, SaaS-based insurance software, has announced the launch of Sapiens Brain, the proprietary AI foundation powering SapiensAIP, its AI platform for the insurance industry. In September 2026, Sapiens launched its AI-native Sapiens Autonomous Insurance Platform (SapiensAIP) , a SaaS solution designed to help insurers integrate AI directly into their core policy administration systems (PAS). Sapiens Brain gives the model the insurance-specific memory that’s grounded, cited and hallucination-resistant by construction enabling it to reason accurately, consistently and with explainability, which is exactly the standard this industry demands.” Sapiens revealed that it decided to build SapiensAIP and the agents that run on Sapiens Brain outside of its core insurance systems.

item.title: Global M&A activity increases in 9M’26, reports WTW
item.description: Global mergers and acquisitions (M&A) activity increased in the first nine months of 2026, with higher-value transactions contributing to a rise in overall deal value, according to WTW, the global professional services company providing risk, insurance, investment and consulting services. WTW reported that activity accelerated during the third quarter, with nine mega deals completed compared with three in the previous quarter. Activity among deals valued between USD $1 billion and USD $10 billion was more subdued.

item.title: So. Korean Banks Were Likely Hacked by China-Based Actor With AI Agent: CrowdStrike
item.description: The suspect behind recent cyberattacks at South Korean banks was likely a China-based 26-year-old who used a Chinese-developed AI agent and Anthropic’s Claude Code, US cybersecurity company CrowdStrike said. In a report published on Wednesday, CrowdStrike said it believed the suspect was likely based in China’s Guangdong province after uncovering personal details linked to the suspected attacker while analyzing AI coding-tool sessions and infrastructure associated with the hacking campaign. At least nine South Korean banks have disclosed or have been reported by local media as having been targeted by cyberattacks since late September, prompting South Korean police to launch a probe this week and President Lee Jae Myung to call for robust response measures.

item.title: TikTok Accused by NY of Running Secret Safety Tests on Teens
item.description: New York Attorney General Letitia James has added new allegations to a child safety lawsuit against TikTok Inc., accusing the platform of running secret experiments on teen users. For the experiment, TikTok withheld a new safety feature from 10% of US users in order to test whether the change reduced user time on the platform. “As a result, TikTok has subjected users whom TikTok included in such A/B tests to an experience that TikTok has made less safe by design,” James said in the amended lawsuit , which includes details of the experiment that were previously sealed from public view.

item.title: Hackers Tricked ASOS Employee to Steal Work Account Login
item.description: ASOS Plc said a recent data breach occurred when an “unauthorized party” impersonated a trusted contact to dupe an employee at the online fashion retailer into handing over log-in details for their work account. The hackers, calling themselves the Xuanye Group, then used those credentials to access information on certain third-party platforms used by ASOS, the UK company said Thursday in an update to customers. The hackers have access to some personal information, including names and contact details, but no payment card information or account passwords were accessed, it said.

item.title: Amica expands partnership with Flume
item.description: Under the expanded partnership with Flume, eligible Amica home policyholders, in participating markets, can enroll to receive a no-cost Flume Smart Home Water Monitor. Along with the sensor, Amica will provide three years of leak monitoring service from Flume. Amica Insurance announced a new program that provides policyholders with access to a smart leak detection monitoring service.

item.title: Benekiva Introduces Kiva Claims Assistant
item.description: (Image source: Benekiva/IIR.) Benekiva (Des Moines, Iowa) has introduced Kiva, an AI Smart Claims Assistant embedded in the company’s Claims Workbench. “We built Kiva to provide another set of eyes within the workflow to help someone recognize a missing requirement or see what needs attention next.” Benekiva positions Kiva as an assistive tool rather than an independent claims decision-maker, with human judgment remaining central to the process. “It should be how much unnecessary work we can take off their plate so they can spend more attention on the decisions and people who need it.” Kiva is available as part of the Benekiva Claims Workbench.

item.title: The Latest Launches from Vertafore, One Inc., Qumis
item.description: Built on the Vertafore VelocityTM AI Platform, Document Intelligence Agent is the latest addition to Vertafore’s growing portfolio of AI agents embedded directly in the workflows insurance professionals use every day. Vertafore, an insurance distribution technology platform, announced general availability of its new Velocity Document Intelligence Agent, which automates research across insurance documents. Qumis, a coverage intelligence platform for commercial property/casualty insurance, introduced Qumis MCP, a new connector designed to bring its insurance-specific intelligence directly into Claude and other AI assistants, applications and enterprise workflows.

item.title: National Flood Insurance Program’s Authority to Expire in December
item.description: The National Flood Insurance Program is once again set to expire in two months. The insurance industry and others – including the National Association of Realtors (NAR) – have been steadfast in lobbying for long-term extensions and reform of the program. The federal flood insurance program has close to 4.5 million flood insurance policies providing almost $1.3 trillion in coverage , said CRS.

item.title: Melwani and James to serve as Co-Heads of UK & Europe Insurance Advisory Partners
item.description: Insurance Advisory Partners (IAP), a boutique investment banking firm specialising in the insurance sector, has appointed Partners Rinki Melwani and Benjamin James as co-heads of UK & Europe. James has deep insurance-sector expertise and a broad advisory and investment background. Throughout his career, he has worked in investment banking and principal investment, including Fenchurch Advisory Partners, Financial Services Capital and Deloitte.

item.title: Fitch upgrades Beazley’s rating, cites strategic importance to Zurich
item.description: The deal creates a huge, global specialty insurance business, with Zurich CEO Mario Greco stating previously that by 2029, “the integration of Beazley will generate incremental revenue growth of over $1 billion per annum.” Fitch’s upgrades reflect its assessment of Beazley’s strategic importance to Zurich, which it determines as ‘Very Important.’ “This results in a two-notch uplift from Beazley’s standalone credit quality of ‘a+’ for its IFS Rating, given ZIG’s stronger credit quality. After Zurich Insurance Group completed its 100% acquisition of specialist insurer Beazley, Fitch Ratings has upgraded the Insurer Financial Strength (IFS) Rating of Beazley Insurance DAC to ‘AA’ from ‘A+’, and also upgraded the Long-Term Issuer Default Ratings (IDRs) of the Dublin subsidiary and Beazley plc to ‘AA-‘ from ‘A’. Today, Fitch, a global credit rating agency, alongside upgrading Beazley Insurance DAC’s IFS Rating and Beazley’s IDRs, has removed the rating from Rating Watch Positive, and confirmed that the outlooks are stable.

item.title: FTC, USDA Seek Comment on Farm Equipment Market Practices
item.description: he Federal Trade Commission and the US Department of Agriculture launched an inquiry into the agricultural equipment market, including potential anticompetitive conduct. That includes a July settlement with Deere, which resolved a lawsuit that alleged the company unlawfully limited the ability of farmers and independent repair providers to service the company’s farm equipment. The public inquiry, announced Wednesday , seeks to address a “growing number of complaints” from farmers that they “face other barriers to acquiring agricultural equipment and the services required to keep equipment operating.” Shares in Deere & Co.

item.title: AM Best Withdraws Credit Ratings of Hartland Mutual
item.description: AM Best has affirmed the Financial Strength Rating of B++ (Good) and the Long-Term Issuer Credit Rating of “bbb+” (Good) of Hartland Mutual Insurance Company (Hartland) (Minot, ND). The ratings reflect Hartland’s balance sheet strength, which AM Best assesses as strong, as well as its adequate operating performance, limited business profile and appropriate enterprise risk management. The outlook of these Credit Ratings (ratings) is stable.

item.title: People Moves: Severino Joins Alliant’s Midwest Benefits Team; Doubtless Names Wiley as Regional President for North America
item.description: Doubtless Names Karl Wiley as Regional President for North America Doubtless, a global pet insurance and solutions organization, has appointed Karl Wiley as North America regional leader, effective October 12, 2026. Jeff Severino has joined Alliant Insurance Services as vice president within its employee benefits group on the Alliant Affinity team. Prior to joining Alliant, Severino was a senior vice president overseeing management liability programs with a national managing general agency.
